PullRequest.Title: Unify sandbox settings and managed policy presentation
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

- Use `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled` across Windows, macOS, and Linux, removing the separate Windows setting and obsolete Agent Host SDK sandbox gates. No migration of the old Windows preference is registered.
- Add Agent Host Copilot controls for local network access, MCP and LSP server sandboxing, and developer-tool access, including restrictive managed-policy handling and session/SDK wiring.
- Improve sandbox setting labels, search keywords, and ordering. Deprecate the auto-approve and retry-with-network controls as local-harness-only; leave the advanced runtime setting non-deprecated.
- Forward effective configuration values, including registered defaults, without inventing defaults for absent optional SDK fields.
- Rename session policy metadata to `vscode.resolvedSandboxPolicy` and move managed Settings UI presentation behind a generic configuration service.
- Update unit tests, picker fixtures, policy documentation, and the Agents Window smoke-test configuration.

## Validation

Passed on the committed sources:

```powershell
.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\services\configuration\test\common\managedSettingsPresentation.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\preferences\test\browser\settingsEditor2.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\preferences\test\browser\settingsTreeModels.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\preferences\test\browser\settingsTree.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\terminalContrib\chatAgentTools\test\common\terminalChatAgentToolsConfiguration.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\services\configuration\test\browser\configurationService.test.ts
```

Result: **156 passed**.

```powershell
npx --no-install eslint src\vs\workbench\contrib\terminalContrib\chatAgentTools\common\terminalChatAgentToolsConfiguration.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\terminalContrib\chatAgentTools\test\common\terminalChatAgentToolsConfiguration.test.ts
git diff --check
git diff --cached --check
```

Result: **all passed**. The existing **Core - Typecheck** watch task reports **0 errors**. Commit-time hygiene checks passed.

Earlier focused validation during implementation also passed: 329 local-network/policy tests, 225 SDK/default-forwarding tests, and `npm run valid-layers-check`. These broader selections were not rerun for the final migration-only removal.

Not run on the final state: a full build, the Agents Window smoke suite, or live provider network/filesystem isolation tests.

## Manual testing

1. Search Settings for `sandbox` and `sandboxing`; inspect labels, ordering, defaults, and local-harness deprecation messages.
2. Enable the unified sandbox setting on Windows, macOS, and Linux; verify both local-harness and Agent Host sessions use it.
3. Apply and remove restrictive managed settings; verify affected settings display enforced values while preserving stored user preferences.
4. Exercise Agent Host session creation, resume, and subsequent requests with network, local-network, bypass, MCP, LSP, and developer-tool settings.

## Notes

- No linked issue was supplied.
- The branch was based on `cbc05014975`; fetched `main` was 41 commits ahead when preparing this draft. No rebase or merge was performed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Settings editor and reflect managed sandbox-policy changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening Settings constructs the delayed presentation service and synchronously scans registered configuration properties before the editor is usable. A later managed-policy or configuration-registry event rescans in process, then only changed setting keys are rerendered. No filesystem, network, subprocess, or IPC operation is invoked by the changed service itself; upstream policy refresh has already completed before its event fires.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of registered configuration properties, typically thousands, plus the small number of properties declaring managedSettingsPresentation (seven in this change). Policy-change frequency is low and registry updates are batched by configuration contribution events.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All projection and rerender scheduling is synchronous on the UI thread; policy events are naturally serialized by the event loop. There is no parallel fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The service builds a cold Map of effective managed values, then retains only defined presentation values. Warm updates still scan the registry but compare against the Map and suppress notifications/rerenders when values are unchanged; no negative-cache ambiguity or unbounded key retention was found.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the full-registry scan and UI-thread reachability; surrounding registry code confirms one event per batched registration/update. The bounded scan and low event frequency do not establish a user-visible regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact configuration-property count and scan duration vary by installed extensions, but work is a shallow object enumeration with only seven callbacks in this diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The generic scan is broader than the previous three-key comparison, but it is lifecycle-bounded, event-driven, suppresses unchanged rerenders, and lacks evidence of meaningful latency or repeated hot-path cost.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and operate Copilot Agent Host permission/sandbox pickers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The changed picker derives the unified setting ID locally, so toggle availability and rendering no longer wait for host OS diagnostics.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHostOperatingSystem.ts:getAgentHostOperatingSystem, formerly reached from the deleted picker lines
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request Agent Host network diagnostics to discover the host OS
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before: one coalesced diagnostics request per connection, with retries after failures; after: zero requests from both changed picker paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Both picker implementations called the shared OS-diagnostics helper; the diff removes those calls and associated retry listeners.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Before, sandbox toggle identity/refresh could wait for the remote diagnostics response; after, setting identity is available synchronously.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One picker/delegate per active chat surface or session; connections may be local or remote.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new async work. The removed helper previously coalesced pending/successful diagnostics per connection with a WeakMap and retried only failures.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Before the diff, host OS diagnostics were positively cached per connection; failures removed the cache entry. After the diff, that cache and lookup are not reached from these pickers.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: deleted call paths and tests explicitly change expected diagnostics request counts from one/retries to zero.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote-host latency varied, but this is an improvement rather than a regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The diff removes an IPC dependency and related asynchronous refresh work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Forward sandbox settings to connected Agent Hosts and apply SDK policy at session launch and each turn
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On connection/schema availability or a sandbox-setting change, the workbench computes one desired sandbox object and dispatches it to each connected host only when unequal. Session launch and each SDK turn then serialize one sandbox options update before progress. The diff adds a few boolean fields to existing objects without increasing update count.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch RootConfigChanged with the sandbox object to an Agent Host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one dispatch per live connection on initial schema availability and per relevant effective setting change; equality suppresses unchanged pushes. The diff adds keys but no calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same one-per-connection dispatch path already forwarded enablement, network, bypass, and filesystem settings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial host configuration must arrive before the host uses the forwarded settings; configuration-change pushes are asynchronous dispatches and not multiplied per setting key.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Call Copilot SDK session.rpc.options.update with sandboxConfig
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One update during session finalization and one serialized update before each turn or relevant config reconciliation, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Sandbox configuration was already applied at launch, before each turn, and after relevant configuration changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The RPC is on launch/turn critical paths, but the diff only enriches its constant-size payload with optional booleans and does not add an RPC.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of live Agent Host connections for workbench forwarding, and number of session launches/turns/config changes for SDK updates. Configuration payload growth is constant (four optional booleans).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Workbench dispatch iterates live connections synchronously with no limiter, as before. Per-session SDK sandbox updates are serialized by _sandboxConfigSequencer; separate sessions may proceed concurrently, unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Workbench caches the desired settings object until a relevant configuration change and deep-compares against each host root state. SDK configuration is recomputed per required update; filesystem path sets are deduplicated during construction. No new unbounded cache or missed coalescing was introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the forwarder, launcher, per-turn preparation, and sequencer call paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: SDK processing cost of individual new flags is not visible in-repository, but no changed call cardinality or scaling input supports a regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Boundary counts, sequencing, and effective cardinality are unchanged; richer constant-size metadata alone is insufficient.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run terminal commands under unified sandbox enablement, including Windows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When the unified setting is on, sandbox prerequisite checks and first-use configuration generation precede wrapped command execution. The first configuration is cached per engine; commands then use the existing sandbox runtime/MXC path. The diff intentionally makes Windows consume the same enablement setting.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the sandbox JSON configuration file on first use or forced refresh
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cached file creation per engine in the normal case; no per-command rewrite unless existing force-refresh conditions apply.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same work occurred when the platform-specific Windows setting or shared non-Windows setting enabled sandboxing; the diff changes which setting selects the existing path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: First sandboxed command waits for policy/path resolution and file creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch commands through the existing sandbox runtime or Windows MXC containment
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sandboxed execution per terminal command while enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Windows used this path when enabledWindows was on; other platforms used it when the shared setting was on. The diff deliberately unifies selection rather than adding another wrapper layer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Sandbox wrapper startup is on command execution, inherent to enabled sandbox semantics.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One first-use setup per sandbox engine plus sandbox wrapper execution per command; filesystem policy work scales with configured paths/workspace roots as before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing engine promises/caches serialize first-use runtime/config state; command execution concurrency is owned by existing terminal/session machinery and is not changed here.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: OS/runtime info, dependency status, temporary directory, and sandbox config path are cached. Force refresh occurs only for explicit refresh or marked configuration changes. Cold Windows users newly covered by unified enablement pay normal sandbox setup; warm commands reuse cached policy/config state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in first-use caching and existing per-command sandbox boundary; there is no diff-introduced duplicate setup or boundary fan-out.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Sandbox startup overhead varies by OS and runtime, but it is the intended cost of enabling the existing security feature and no bounded behavior-preserving optimization is exposed by the changed hunks.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Unified Windows enablement changes feature applicability intentionally, while the underlying cached setup and per-command boundary are unchanged and not duplicated.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 53 changed files and every diff page. Traced Settings UI projection, picker diagnostics, workbench-to-host forwarding, SDK sandbox updates, and terminal sandbox execution. No high-confidence, actionable performance regression was introduced; notable boundary work is unchanged or reduced.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
